chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran — or someone else — from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said:

I asked him about the divorce of the Sunnah. He said: The divorce of the Sunnah is that when a man intends to divorce his wife, he leaves her — if he has consummated the marriage — until she menstruates and then becomes pure. When she becomes pure, he divorces her once with the testimony of two witnesses, then leaves her until she observes an 'iddah of three menstrual cycles. When the three cycles have passed, she is irrevocably separated from him by one (divorce), and her ex-husband becomes a suitor among suitors: if she wishes, she may marry him, and if she wishes, she may not. If he marries her with a new dowry, she is with him with two (divorces) remaining and one having passed.

If he then divorces her with another (divorce) in a state of purity and without intercourse, with the testimony of two witnesses, then leaves her until her menstrual cycles pass — if her cycles pass before he returns to her — she is irrevocably separated from him by two (divorces), she controls her own affairs, and she is free to marry. Her ex-husband is a suitor among suitors: if she wishes she may marry him, if she wishes she may not. If he marries her with a new marriage and new dowry, she is with him with one (divorce) remaining and two having passed. If he intends to divorce her with a divorce after which she is not lawful for him until she marries another husband, he leaves her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then has witnessed against her divorce one pronouncement — then she is not lawful for him until she marries another husband.

As for the revocable divorce (talaq al-raj'ah): he leaves her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then divorces her with the testimony of two witnesses, then returns to her and has intercourse with her, then waits with her for purity. When she menstruates and becomes pure, he has two witnesses witness another divorce. Then he returns to her and has intercourse with her, then waits with her for purity. When she menstruates and becomes pure, he has two witnesses witness the third divorce. Then she is never lawful for him until she marries another husband, and it is upon her to observe an 'iddah of three menstrual cycles from the day he pronounced the third divorce.

If he divorces her once in a state of purity with witnesses, then waits with her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then divorces her before he returns to her — his second divorce is not a valid divorce because he is divorcing a divorcee. For when the woman is divorced from her husband, she is outside his ownership until he returns to her. When he returns to her, she comes under his ownership so long as he has not pronounced the third divorce. When he pronounces the third divorce, the right of reversion has left his hands. If he divorces her in a state of purity with witnesses, then returns to her and waits with her for purity without intercourse, then she menstruates and becomes pure, then he divorces her before violating her by intercourse after the reversion — his divorce of her is not a valid divorce, because he divorced her with the second pronouncement in the first purity, and purity is not nullified except by intercourse after the reversion. And similarly, the third divorce does not occur except through a reversion and intercourse after the reversion, then menstruation and purity after the menstruation, then a divorce with witnesses — so that each divorce has a purity free from the violation of intercourse, witnessed.

key_terms.الطُّهْرُ: Purity (between two menstrual cycles) — the required state in which divorce must be pronounced
key_terms.الْبَيْنُونَةُ: Bainunah — irrevocable separation of the spouses following completion of 'iddah
key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ / الْقُرُوءُ: The 'iddah — the waiting period of three menstrual cycles that a divorced woman must observe before remarrying
key_terms.الْمَهْرُ الْجَدِيدُ: New dowry — required for remarriage after a completed irrevocable divorce
key_terms.الْمُرَاجَعَةُ: Raj'ah (reversion) — the husband's act of returning to the wife during the revocable divorce period
key_terms.الْمُوَاقَعَةُ: Sexual intercourse — which, after reversion, establishes a new state of purity required before the next divorce
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ شَاهِدَيْنِ: Testimony of two witnesses — a necessary condition for a valid divorce pronouncement in Shia law
key_terms.طَلَاقُ الرَّجْعَةِ: Talaq al-raj'ah — revocable divorce, where the husband retains the right to return to the wife before completion of 'iddah
key_terms.طَلَاقُ السُّنَّةِ: Talaq al-sunnah — divorce according to Prophetic practice, performed in a state of purity without intercourse, with two witnesses

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for talaq al-sunnah and talaq al-raj'ah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a comprehensive legal ruling on the two types of divorce in Islamic law: talaq al-sunnah (divorce according to the Prophetic practice) and talaq al-raj'ah (revocable divorce). He details the precise procedural requirements — waiting for purity, the necessity of witnesses, the counting of 'iddah periods, and the conditions under which remarriage is permitted. This hadith was transmitted through Abu Baseer, a leading companion of the Imams, and reflects the careful jurisprudential tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt in defining lawful family dissolution.
